title: Validate bare work-item and task IDs as references
objective: Make sdlc ref validate accept bare repository-local work-item IDs such as WI-0001 and canonical task UIDs such as WI-0001-80000000 through the dynamic reference-schema registry.

branch.name: main
branch.rationale: The repository is already on the main branch and the user requested preparation, processing, and per-task commits on the current repository.

request.text: Review the unexpected behavior where sdlc ref validate rejects bare work-item IDs such as WI-0001 and bare canonical task IDs such as WI-0001-80000000 even though sdlc task list can discover those objects. Prepare a new .docs/work-items/* and commit the work item. Process the new work item, commit per task.

scope.name: bare-work-item-reference
scope.description: Register the canonical WorkItemId string grammar as a supported direct reference for sdlc ref validate.
scope.reason: Operators need to validate a bare work-item identity without adding a file or selector suffix.

scope.name: bare-task-reference
scope.description: Register the canonical task UID grammar, including its work-item prefix and eight-digit order key, as a supported direct reference for sdlc ref validate.
scope.reason: Task discovery exposes canonical task UIDs such as WI-0001-80000000 and the same identity should be accepted by direct reference validation.

scope.name: dynamic-reference-coverage
scope.description: Preserve recursive discovery of marked reference schemas and exercise the new bare-ID examples through the existing dynamic test boundary.
scope.reason: Future direct reference types must remain covered without hardcoded validator or test lists.

scope.name: reference-contract-documentation
scope.description: Document that marked identifier schemas may participate in direct reference validation and update the response contract examples.
scope.reason: The registry convention must explain why identity schemas are marked and make the accepted forms discoverable.

nonGoals.name: target-resolution
nonGoals.description: Do not make sdlc ref validate resolve the supplied bare ID to an existing work-item or task file.
nonGoals.reason: The existing command contract is syntactic schema matching; object resolution belongs to work-item validation or another future command.

nonGoals.name: qualified-reference-change
nonGoals.description: Do not change the existing local, task-qualified, global, or task-specific entity reference grammars except where contract examples must acknowledge the new direct identifier forms.
nonGoals.reason: The defect is limited to bare identity forms and existing qualified references already work.

nonGoals.name: version-release
nonGoals.description: Do not bump the package version as part of this work item.
nonGoals.reason: The user requested the behavior fix and task commits but did not request a release-version change; versioning can be handled by a separate release work item.

items.name: bare-work-item-id
items.description: sdlc ref validate must accept a bare WorkItemId matching the repository WorkItemId grammar.
items.reason: A work-item identity is a valid direct reference input for operators and automation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: sdlc ref validate --ref WI-0001 returns exit code zero and identifies the registered work-item ID schema.

items.name: bare-task-uid
items.description: sdlc ref validate must accept a bare canonical task UID matching the task envelope UID grammar, including a work-item prefix and eight-digit order key.
items.reason: Task list exposes canonical UIDs and callers should not need to construct a qualified entity selector to validate the identity.

acceptanceCriteria.description: sdlc ref validate --ref WI-0001-80000000 returns exit code zero and identifies the registered task UID schema.
Malformed task UID strings and pipe-qualified identifiers outside the bare UID grammar are not incorrectly accepted by the task UID schema.

items.name: dynamic-registry-coverage
items.description: The implementation must use the existing recursive x-sdlc-reference-type registry convention and dynamically exercise every marked schema example.
items.reason: The registry must remain extensible without hardcoded schema or reference-type lists.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The dynamic reference test validates every root example, including the new bare work-item and task UID examples, and existing marked reference examples continue to pass.

items.name: read-only-reference-validation
items.description: The command and tests must remain read-only and must retain the existing syntactic-only response contract.
items.reason: Direct reference validation must not mutate or require resolution of the selected repository objects.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Fresh-process validation from the sdlc repository and a separate repository returns stable JSON, leaves repository state unchanged, and preserves existing qualified-reference behavior.
